title: LAMOST-calibrated Gaia XP metallicities of 67 main-sequence dust dimmers give a metallicity exponent of 0.85 (95 %: 0 to 1.8): dimmers are not metal-poor, and beta = 2 is disfavoured but not excluded
abstract: Question: Is deep dust dimming of main-sequence stars more frequent at high metallicity, as giant-planet occurrence is (P proportional to 10^(beta [Fe/H]), beta 1.2-2), or is it independent of metallicity, as debris discs are? Approach: We took 92 dimmers (81 ZTF dippers of Tzanidakis et al. 2025 and 11 campaign dust dimmers). For 67 of them, we compared the Gaia XP [Fe/H] of Zhang, Green and Rix (2023) with 21,908 Gaia DR3 field stars of the same field, colour, parallax and absolute G. We measured the XP errors with 773 LAMOST DR10 dwarfs in 15 dimmer fields and used a kernel calibration in a matched-set likelihood for beta. Results: The dimmers are not metal-poor. Their mean XP [Fe/H] rank is 0.558 (expected 0.5; z = 1.66), and the mean offset is +0.04 dex (95 %: -0.04 to +0.12). Against LAMOST, XP [Fe/H] has 0.20 dex robust scatter and a metal-poor outlier tail, so beta = 2 predicts a mean rank of only 0.66. The calibrated exponent is 0.85 (95 %: -0.02 to 1.81) for all dimmers and 0.55 (-0.32 to 1.47) for the ZTF dippers; beta = 2 has likelihood ratios 0.06 and 0.014. Other matching choices give beta 0.25-1.45 and some allow beta = 2. In Gaia DR3 (2014-2017), 40 percent of the dimmers (34 percent of the ZTF dippers, p = 2e-7) are in the bottom decile of photometric precision of their field, and XP fits have higher chi-square and extinction (z = 3.3 and 3.4). Gaia epoch data show fading dips in 3 of 11 variable dimmers; 7 others are RS CVn or solar-like spot variables. Limitations: no dimmer has a LAMOST spectrum, the LAMOST service went offline after 17 fields, and the ZTF dipper sample includes spot variables.
